Tone and outlook: The March 16, 2022 FOMC statement is hawkish (rate liftoff, balance-sheet runoff) in response to elevated inflation and uncertainty from the Russia–Ukraine invasion. The February 2022 Beige Book reports moderate expansion but widespread supply constraints and worker shortages, with Omicron-related absenteeism disrupting activity in several districts (e.g., New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Chicago, San Francisco). Wage and price pressures were broad-based, and many firms passed higher input costs to customers. Manufacturing continued to grow, but consumer-facing sectors—especially hospitality—saw softer demand during the Omicron wave. Layering in SLOOS: banks eased standards and saw stronger C&I demand (supporting business investment), but they reported weaker demand for residential real estate/GSE mortgages and expect some deterioration in household credit quality (credit cards, autos, nonconforming jumbos) as rates rise. Net: business credit resilience offsets some downside risk, but inflation, labor/supply frictions, and consumer/housing headwinds keep a cautious-hawkish stance with a slight negative tilt.
